title: Best AI Cold Calling Software 2026
summary: A tested, ranked comparison of seven AI cold calling platforms for sales teams replacing manual dialers in 2026. SigmaMind AI leads for call centers that want to layer AI onto an existing dialer (VICIdial, Five9, NICE, Genesys) with transparent per-minute pricing and no concurrency fees. Retell AI and Vapi suit engineering-led teams building custom infrastructure, Bland AI fits developer-supported programs with committed pricing tiers, Synthflow AI and CloudTalk serve smaller or SMB teams wanting fast no-code or per-seat setups, and Thoughtly is positioned honestly as better suited to opted-in lead re-engagement than pure cold outbound. Each entry covers pricing, CRM integration depth, voicemail detection, and conversation quality, with a comparison table up top and use-case callouts for high-volume dialing, objection handling, real estate prospecting, SDR teams, and insurance agencies.

## TL;DR


- **SigmaMind AI** adds AI to VICIdial, Five9, NICE, or Genesys and charges a $0.04-per-minute platform fee without concurrency fees.
- **Retell AI** suits developer-led builds that need API-first voice infrastructure.
- **Bland AI** fits developer-supported, high-volume calling programs that need programmable controls and committed pricing tiers.
- **Vapi** gives engineering-led enterprises configurable voice infrastructure but requires substantial technical setup.
- **Synthflow AI** offers fast no-code setup for general-purpose voice agents and smaller agencies.
- **CloudTalk** gives SMB sales groups a per-seat dialer with broad CRM support.
- **Thoughtly** fits opted-in lead re-engagement better than pure cold prospecting.


[See how SigmaMind AI works](https://dashboard.sigmamind.ai/p/signup) with existing dialers and usage-based pricing without concurrency charges.


## Why cold calling teams are turning to AI dialers


Sales reps spend much of a manual dialing shift reaching voicemail, unanswered lines, or gatekeepers. A[Brilo comparison of manual and parallel dialers](https://www.brilo.ai/resources/best-ai-cold-calling-software) estimates that a rep may complete 60 to 100 manual dials per day, while a parallel dialer may attempt 300 to 500 numbers by calling several contacts at once and routing live answers to a rep.


AI cold calling software can take over more of that work by detecting voicemail, speaking with prospects, handling common objections, and transferring qualified contacts to a closer. B2B SDR teams can then spend more time on active conversations instead of repeated dialing.


We tested each platform for outbound calling, focusing on conversation quality, voicemail detection, CRM and dialer integrations, high-concurrency pricing, and transfer handling.


## What to look for in AI cold calling software


**Pricing transparency and concurrency.** Calculate the full per-minute cost, including voice, language model, telephony, transfer, and simultaneous-call fees.


**CRM and dialer integrations.** Check whether the software connects directly to your current tools and writes structured call outcomes without middleware.


**Voicemail detection.** Test whether the agent reliably distinguishes live answers, voicemail greetings, IVR menus, and disconnected numbers before billing or triggering follow-up.


**Conversational quality.** Call the agent yourself and assess pacing, interruptions, latency, and responses to pricing objections. Effective agents follow qualification logic while responding to what the prospect actually said. Thoughtly includes conversational responsiveness in its[comparison criteria for outbound voice agents](https://thoughtly.com/blog/best-ai-voice-agents-for-outbound-sales-calls-2026) .


**Compliance controls.** Confirm that the platform can store consent records, screen do-not-call lists, restrict calling hours, and manage caller ID. Because federal rules treat AI-generated voices as artificial or prerecorded calls, review each campaign under applicable federal and state requirements.

### SigmaMind AI


**Best for**


SigmaMind AI ranks first for call centers that want outbound AI calling on existing dialers such as VICIdial, Five9, NICE, or Genesys. It also suits B2B SDR operations that need to qualify large lead lists and transfer interested prospects to human reps.


**What it is**


[SigmaMind AI](https://sigmamind.ai/) adds voice agents to an existing dialer and telephony stack. You can add SigmaMind AI without replacing the dialer or rebuilding its connected workflows.


SigmaMind AI charges by usage without concurrency fees. The platform rate remains the same per minute regardless of the number of simultaneous calls, although total usage still increases as more calls run.


The no-code workflow builder supports node-level function calls for multi-step qualification and objection handling. A built-in voicemail detection engine separates voicemail from live answers, while warm and cold transfers pass the full conversation context to a human rep.


**Pros**


- SigmaMind AI integrates with established dialers and connects with CRMs, schedulers, payment tools, and internal systems through prebuilt integrations or APIs.
- Ops staff can change qualification flows without engineering support, while developers can use APIs and MCP tools for custom deployments.
- Warm transfers give reps the lead’s answers and prior conversation, which reduces repetition after an AI agent identifies an interested prospect.
- The model-agnostic stack lets you choose speech, voice, and language-model providers based on cost, language, or conversation quality.


**Cons**


- SigmaMind AI offers APIs and MCP support, but its developer ecosystem remains less mature than developer-first infrastructure products such as Retell AI or Vapi.
- Buyers must calculate several usage layers to estimate the final per-minute cost.
- Call centers without an existing outbound operation may prefer a simpler general-purpose builder with fewer deployment choices.


**Pricing**


SigmaMind AI charges a $0.04 per-minute platform fee with no subscription or concurrency charge on its pay-as-you-go plan. The full voice cost combines that fee with speech-to-text, text-to-speech, a language model, and telephony.


The stated component estimates include $0.01 per minute for Deepgram speech recognition, $0.01 to $0.06 per minute for voice generation, and $0.003 to $0.06 per minute for the language model. The stated Twilio rate adds $0.015 per minute. SigmaMind AI does not add a telephony fee when customers connect custom telephony or SIP trunking. Enterprise customers receive custom volume pricing.


### Retell AI


**Best for**


Retell AI fits engineering-led sales teams that want control over voice infrastructure and can build the CRM, calendar, and campaign layers around it.


**What it is**


Retell AI ranks second as a developer-first platform rather than a finished cold-calling operations product. In our testing, its API and webhooks let technical users configure model choice, voice providers, and call routing.


**Pros**


- Retell AI lets you choose the language model, voice provider, and telephony connection for each deployment.
- API access and webhooks support custom qualification logic and data handling.
- Retell AI includes 20 concurrent calls on self-serve plans, which gives smaller deployments room to test outbound workloads.


**Cons**


- Retell AI lacks a native CRM and calendar, so you must connect external tools through APIs or automation middleware.
- A third-party[HubSpot Marketplace connector](https://ecosystem.hubspot.com/marketplace/listing/cetdigit-retell-ai) provides the closest option to native CRM support, but available documentation does not confirm equivalent built-in support for other CRMs.
- Extra concurrency costs $8 per slot each month. Available sources do not independently document voicemail detection performance for cold-calling campaigns.


**Pricing**


Retell AI uses layered consumption pricing. The voice engine starts at $0.07 per minute, while the selected language model and telephony provider add separate charges. A typical configuration with a mid-range model and managed Twilio costs about $0.105 per minute, while premium configurations can reach roughly $0.175 per minute.[Reported production costs commonly fall between $0.11 and $0.15 per minute](https://zeeg.me/en/blog/post/retell-ai-pricing-guide) . Buyers should calculate the full stack rather than compare platforms against Retell AI’s voice-engine rate alone.


### Bland AI


**Best for**


Bland AI fits developer-supported call operations that value programmable controls and expect enough volume to benefit from committed pricing tiers. Buyers in regulated industries should verify that its compliance controls meet their legal and security requirements.


**What it is**


Bland AI provides API-first infrastructure for building inbound and outbound voice agents. Its programmatic call flows and webhook support let developers customize call behavior, but deployment requires more technical work than a finished sales operations product.


**Pros**


Bland AI supports custom call logic, voice cloning, and warm transfers. Its higher tiers raise daily call and concurrency limits for larger outbound programs. Bringing your own Twilio number can remove certain attempt and transfer charges.


**Cons**


Bland AI does not publish a clear native CRM connector list in the available sources, so you may need API or webhook work. Buyers should also model voicemail costs because Bland bills voicemail at the full connected-minute rate.


**Pricing**


Bland AI uses a[four-tier pricing structure](https://zeeg.me/en/blog/post/bland-ai-pricing) . Start charges no monthly fee and $0.14 per connected minute. Build costs $299 monthly plus $0.12 per minute, while Scale costs $499 monthly plus $0.11 per minute. Enterprise pricing is custom. Transfers cost $0.05, $0.04, or $0.03 per minute across the first three tiers. Bland also charges a $0.015 minimum for each outbound attempt on its telephony, including failed calls, while customers using their own Twilio numbers avoid that minimum.


### Vapi


**Best for**


Vapi ranks fourth and suits enterprises with engineering resources that want configurable infrastructure for custom outbound AI calling.


**What it is**


Vapi supplies API-driven voice components rather than a finished sales operations product. You must configure Vapi's voice components and connect them to your outbound workflow, so deployment requires more engineering than the other top-four options.


Available[comparison data](https://www.brilo.ai/resources/best-voice-ai-for-outbound-sales-calls) lists CRM synchronization as API-based. You will likely need developers to connect lead records, call dispositions, and follow-up actions. Conversation quality also depends on how well you configure prompts and call logic rather than arriving tuned for cold calling.


**Pros**


- Developers can control voice behavior, call flows, and integrations through APIs.
- The configurable foundation supports complex outbound workflows and enterprise deployments.
- Vapi supports speed-to-lead use cases that trigger calls after a prospect submits information.


**Cons**


- API-based CRM synchronization requires more engineering work than native connectors.
- Cold-call conversation quality depends heavily on your configuration.
- Independent sources do not document Vapi’s voicemail detection capabilities in enough detail to assess high-volume voicemail handling.


**Pricing**


One independent comparison lists Vapi at a starting platform rate of $0.05 per minute. Treat that figure as directional because Vapi’s current total cost may include telephony, model, and voice charges. Available sources do not confirm concurrency fees or a complete component-level breakdown.


### Synthflow AI


**Best for**


Synthflow AI ranks fifth and best suits small businesses or agencies that want to launch voice agents without writing code.


**What it is**


Synthflow AI is a general-purpose, no-code voice agent builder for inbound and outbound calls. In our evaluation, its visual builder made basic agents easy to configure, but the product felt less tailored to large cold-calling campaigns. A[HappyRobot comparison describes its dialer and campaign tools as “noticeably lighter” than those of outbound-focused platforms](https://www.happyrobot.ai/hub/synthflow-reviews-and-pricing) .


**Pros**


- The visual builder helps you launch call flows without engineering support.
- Synthflow AI reports connections with more than 200 CRM, scheduling, and automation tools.
-


**Cons**


- High-volume outbound teams may outgrow the campaign and dialer controls.
- The base plan includes five concurrent calls, and each additional slot costs $20 per month.
- Complex CRM workflows may require Zapier or Make as middleware.


**Pricing**


Synthflow AI combines a $0.09 per-minute voice engine with LLM and telephony charges. LLM usage adds $0.02 to $0.05 per minute, while managed Twilio adds $0.02 per minute.[The resulting base cost typically reaches $0.11 to $0.16 per minute](https://zeeg.me/en/blog/post/synthflow-ai-pricing) , depending on the model and telephony setup. Performance routing and low-latency routing each add $0.04 per minute.


### CloudTalk


**Best for**


CloudTalk fits SMB sales teams that want outbound AI calling within a familiar business phone system.


**What it is**


CloudTalk combines a per-seat phone platform with power, preview, and parallel dialers. In our evaluation, it behaved more like a SaaS dialer with optional AI than a dedicated AI-agent platform. CloudTalk provides fewer documented controls for complex AI-led objection handling than SigmaMind AI, Retell AI, or Bland AI.


**Pros**


CloudTalk supports answering machine detection and voicemail drop, which reduces time spent on unanswered calls. Its[100-plus integrations](https://www.cloudtalk.io/pricing/) include HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho CRM, Salesforce, Salesloft, and Outreach.


**Cons**


CloudTalk reserves several outbound features for higher tiers or paid add-ons. Salesforce requires the Expert plan, while parallel dialing costs extra. The modular pricing can make total outbound costs harder to forecast.


**Pricing**


[Starter costs $25 per user monthly](https://www.nextiva.com/blog/cloudtalk-pricing.html) with annual billing, Essential costs $29, and Expert costs $49. Monthly billing raises those prices to $34, $39, and $69. AI Conversation Intelligence adds $9 per user monthly, and the parallel dialer adds $39. AI Voice Agents cost $350 monthly for 1,000 minutes, with $0.50 per-minute overages.


### Thoughtly


**Best for**


Thoughtly best suits businesses re-engaging form fills, missed inbound callers, aged pipeline leads, and appointment requests.


**What it is**


Thoughtly combines voice calling with SMS, email, WhatsApp, and CRM write-back. In our evaluation, its multichannel design made the most sense for leads who had already contacted a business.


Thoughtly’s own comparison page[says it does not support cold outbound](https://thoughtly.com/blog/thoughtly-vs-air-ai-comparison) . Thoughtly positions the product for converting opted-in demand rather than calling cold lists.


**Pros**


Thoughtly supports bidirectional connections with HubSpot, Salesforce, GoHighLevel, Pipedrive, and Zoho. Its agents detect voicemail, leave messages, and can trigger follow-up texts. The platform also supports branching qualification logic and interruption handling.


**Cons**


Thoughtly does not fit pure cold-call prospecting or purchased-list campaigns. Real estate teams calling expired listings or FSBO leads and SDR groups replacing manual cold dialing should consider a platform built for those outbound workloads.


The available sources provide no independent conversation-quality benchmark or published voicemail-detection accuracy rate.


**Pricing**


Thoughtly uses per-minute billing but does not publish its rate, concurrency terms, or standard tiers. The company[quotes pricing based on volume and channels](https://thoughtly.com/blog/best-ai-voice-agents-for-outbound-sales-calls-2026) , so buyers must contact sales for a cost estimate.


## Matching the platform to your use case


**High-volume dialing.** SigmaMind AI fits high-volume campaigns that run many calls concurrently through an existing dialer. Its voicemail detection separates recordings from live answers, while its no-concurrency-fee pricing keeps parallel calling bursts from triggering added platform charges.


**Live objection handling.** Retell AI suits engineering-led sales groups that want to encode objection branches and connect their own CRM tools. In our testing, its API-first approach offered more technical control, but you need engineering resources to build and maintain the surrounding sales workflow.


**Real estate prospecting.** Synthflow AI offers a no-code option for smaller agencies calling expired listings and for-sale-by-owner leads. Its visual builder reduces setup work, but buyers should verify that Synthflow AI supports their property data provider, consent records, and required list-screening process.


**B2B SDR teams.** SigmaMind AI can handle initial qualification and transfer interested prospects to a rep with the full conversation context. Its node-level workflow builder supports multi-step qualification, so SDRs spend less time dialing and more time handling qualified conversations.


**Insurance agencies.** SigmaMind AI directly fits consent-qualified lead lists that expand during open enrollment or renewal season. The platform can call leads concurrently, detect interest, and transfer suitable prospects to licensed agents without concurrency charges. Bland AI also merits consideration when an agency has developers available and prioritizes programmable call controls over existing-dialer integration.

## How we evaluated these platforms


We evaluated each platform through hands-on testing of setup, outbound call flows, objection handling, voicemail detection, and transfers to human representatives. We also compared pricing transparency, concurrency charges, CRM and dialer integrations, workflow controls, and the technical effort required for deployment.


We checked pricing, integration, and feature claims against vendor documentation and the third-party sources linked throughout the article. Rankings reflect suitability for AI cold calling rather than general voice agent capability. We gave more weight to reliable outbound operations, predictable costs, and practical call-center integration than to broad feature counts.


## Frequently asked questions


**Is AI cold calling legal?**


AI cold calling is subject to consent, disclosure, calling-hour, and do-not-call requirements, and the applicable rules vary by campaign and jurisdiction. Federal rules treat AI-generated voices as artificial or prerecorded voice calls, as summarized in this[overview of AI cold-calling compliance](https://www.outreach.ai/resources/blog/ai-cold-calling) . SigmaMind AI lets users configure campaigns around applicable requirements, but users should obtain legal guidance for their specific calling program.


**How much does AI cold calling software cost?**


AI cold calling software usually combines platform, voice, language model, and telephony charges. SigmaMind AI charges a $0.04 per-minute platform fee without concurrency charges, while other providers may use layered usage pricing or volume tiers. Buyers should calculate costs across attempted calls, voicemail connections, transfers, and simultaneous calls.


**Can AI cold calling fully replace human SDRs?**


AI cold calling can handle prospecting tasks such as dialing, basic objection handling, qualification, and routing. SigmaMind AI can transfer qualified prospects to human SDRs with the conversation context attached. Human reps remain better suited to complex negotiations, relationship-based selling, and closing.
